title: When lonely
hookLine: He is closer than the jugular vein (50:16)
tomorrow: Amira missed a deadline. what's wrong with saying 'if only'?

lines: TEN AT NIGHT. THE FRIDGE HUMS.
cards: Ten at night. Dad's closing the shop late, a grandmother is asleep in a hospital chair beside her friend, and the house has that particular quiet where you can hear the fridge.
A phone full of group chats, and nobody to actually call. Lonely isn't always about an empty room. It's about distance: how far away is anyone who'd notice?
The Qur'an answers that question with a measurement. A strange one. You can find it with two fingers.

teach.b: It's in Surah Qaf, in Pickthall's translation: "We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein."
The jugular is the big vein at the side of your neck, the one you can feel beating. You can't get much closer than that without being you.

teach.h: HE KNOWS WHAT THE SOUL WHISPERS.
teach.b: And look at what the verse says God knows: not only your words, but what your soul whispers.
Commentators read the nearness in more than one way: some say it's His knowledge, some say the angels who record; none reads it as a body in your neck. Then a second verse, in Surah al-Baqarah.
Nearby, people ask the Prophet things, and the answer begins with say: they ask about the new moons; say. Here, the question is about God himself, and there's no say.
God answers directly: "And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me."
None of this says people don't matter.
A quiet house still deserves a phone call. But under the lonely night is a floor, closer than anyone you could call.

how: Muslims turn to du'a, personal prayer in their own words, at any hour and in any language, alongside the five daily prayers; Qur'an 50:16 and 2:186 are often recalled as a reminder that God is near.

o: being alone as a sign that your faith is weak
feeling alone, with God still nearer than your pulse
a feeling that faith should make disappear

games.q: what goes with what — tap the pairs.
p: the big vein at the side of the neck
God's answer when asked about Him
the answer comes straight from God
what the verse says God knows

s: the verse means God is physically inside your body
commentators read it as nearness of knowledge, or of the angels who record; none as a body in your neck.
in 2:186 the answer comes with no 'say' before it
nearby verses answer with 'say'; here God answers the question about Himself directly.

games.q: a friend who just moved away for college says nobody there knows her name yet. what fits today's verses?
o: God's nearness is the floor under her while she finds people; it doesn't replace them.
if she really believed God was near, she wouldn't feel lonely at all.
feeling lonely means she has drifted far from God and needs to fix that first.
games.why: He is nearer than the jugular vein, and still the lesson says a quiet house deserves a phone call. nearness is a floor, not a replacement.

practice: Rest two fingers lightly at the side of your neck, just under the jaw, until you find the pulse. Don't count it; just feel it keep going on its own, with no help from you. The verse puts Him nearer than that.
If you pray, make du'a in your own words for the rest of the sit, the way you'd talk to someone in the room; if not, just stay with the beat.

wordCard.voice: When lonely: the quiet house, the full phone, the distance. The Qur'an says He is nearer than your jugular vein.

orig.note: Arabic: the jugular vein (50:16); habl means a rope or cord.

carryVoice: The line for today: never alone, with Him nearer than the pulse under your fingers. Good night, or good morning.
